doc.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The sponsor tries to ban Billie Holiday from the show
summary: A sponsor's representative objected to Holiday's drug record; Herridge threatened to quit and Billie stayed.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Whitney got me into that. When you think about it, we had Red Allen, Thelonious Monk, Basie, all kinds of people, and I think only one or two of them are stil alive.
Yeah, Joe Wilder I think is the only one.

So it was very fortunate that we had Herridge to – see, that was a Sunday afternoon prime-time show, which meant a lot at the time. During that soundtrack thing, a page came over to Herridge with a note. He looked at it and tore it up. I said to him afterward, “What was that?” He said, “The sponsor’s representative said he did not want a woman coming into the homes of America on a Sunday afternoon who had been in prison on a drug charge.” Herridge sent back a note saying, “If Billie Holiday isn’t on the show, I’m leaving the show, so is Whitney Balliett, and so is Hentoff.” That was the end of that.
